text: Was the stranger really lost on the moor?
why: The stranger claims to be lost, but his nervousness, his questions about the lone stable boy, and his bribe give the reader reason to ask whether he was really lost.

text: Was the stranger really lost on the moor? — lost on the moor, as he says

why: This is the stranger's own stated account, and it is a possibility the reader can weigh against what has been shown.

text: Was the stranger really lost on the moor? — he came to the stables on purpose
id: q.stranger_lost=he came to the stables on purpose
why: His knowledge of the stable boy's solitary night and his offer of a bribe give the reader a reason to consider that he came deliberately.

text: What was in the stranger's folded paper?
why: The contents of the folded paper have not been revealed, so asking what it contains is a plain question the story has raised.

text: What was in the stranger's folded paper? — a drug for the boy's supper

why: The stranger ties the paper to the boy's supper and asks that the boy have it tonight, so the reader can reasonably consider something being added to the food. The specific word 'drug' is not stated, but it is a fair possibility to weigh.

text: What was in the stranger's folded paper? — money for the boy
why: The story says the reward of money is for the maid, Edith, not the boy. Nothing so far suggests the boy receives money in the paper.

text: What was in the stranger's folded paper? — a note for the boy
